# What did you know, and when? Answer on demand with bitemporal data


[Prashant Gandhi](https://www.griddynamics.com/author/prashant-gandhi)


[Henry Garner](https://www.griddynamics.com/author/henry-garner)


A regulator asks what your bank held on a given date and what it knew at the time. Most banks answer by rebuilding history from event logs. The process is slow and error-prone, and the scale makes it worse: billions of assets and positions, each with end-of-day adjustments.


A major US investment bank solved this at the data layer. The team added[bitemporal data](https://www.griddynamics.com/blog/bitemporal-data-regulatory-compliance) support to the bank’s key-value store. Every position now carries two timelines: when it was true and when the bank first recorded it. An immutable transaction log keeps both intact.


A GraphQL query layer sits on top. One store serves as a complete historical archive and as a low-latency source for live queries, so teams query history and live data through the same interface.


The bank now reconstructs any end-of-day position, adjustments included, on demand. The audit trail lives in the data model itself, so no separate reporting process produces it. That holds across billions of records.


If your teams still rebuild history for every regulator request, this case study shows a faster path. Read how a bitemporal store turns the next question into a query, then explore Grid Dynamics[financial services technology](https://www.griddynamics.com/industries/financial-services) for banks and capital markets firms.
